title: Machine-learning analysis of plasma metabolomic fingerprints yields a 21-metabolite gastric-cancer panel validated across multicentre cohorts
summary: In a multicentre study, machine-learning analysis of plasma metabolic fingerprints from 1,944 retrospective participants selected a 21-metabolite panel that differentiated gastric-cancer from non-cancer cohorts; five model types achieved AUCs of 0.921–0.971 in discovery and 0.907–0.940 in external verification. Prospective testing in 264 participants using both NPELDI-MS and UPLC-MS reported diagnostic AUCs of 0.855–0.918 and 0.856–0.916, respectively. The paper also reports a four-metabolite prognostic score based on retrospective survival data.
ai_technology: Neural network, lasso regression, ridge regression, support-vector machine and random-forest models applied to plasma metabolic fingerprints
organization: Zhejiang Cancer Hospital; Shanghai Jiao Tong University and six collaborating clinical centers

evidence.tested: In a multicentre study, machine-learning analysis of plasma metabolic fingerprints from 1,944 retrospective participants selected a 21-metabolite panel that differentiated gastric-cancer from non-cancer cohorts; five model types achieved AUCs of 0.921–0.971 in discovery and 0.907–0.940 in external verification.
evidence.unknown: The panel was evaluated in selected clinical cohorts and is not established for routine screening or clinical use. Prospective validation was at one lead center, and only six panel metabolites were robustly detected by confirmatory UPLC-MS under the reported testing. Model performance does not show that the panel is causal or improves outcomes. Primary full text/abstract checked; no independent replication assessed.
evidence.ai_role: The study used machine-learning feature selection/modeling (including logistic-regression coefficient filtering) to identify and evaluate a 21-metabolite diagnostic panel from high-throughput mass-spectrometry fingerprints; classifiers were then validated on independent retrospective and prospective cohorts.
